title: NET-Seq
scope: Churchman 2011 NET-seq implementation in Saccharomyces cerevisiae, extracted at the level of the assigned Illumina NET-Seq schematic. The retained route is RNAPII-complex immunoprecipitation, RNA extraction and reverse transcription to cDNA. The poster NET-Seq row corroborates that route; its DeepCAGE, 3′NT and mNET-seq rows and adjacent structural panel are separate depictions. The introductory polymerase icons identify the assay rather than adding an action or branch. The cap symbol describes the illustrated RNA and does not establish cap selection or universal capping. The final cDNA is a physical sequence carrier, not measured RNA or sequencing data. Detailed library construction and sequencing are described only to interpret the stated 3-prime-end readout, not added as unshown operations.

operations.label: Immunoprecipitate RNAPII elongation complexes
operations.description: Select the RNAPII-complex preparation by immunoprecipitation, retaining associated RNA with the captured complexes. The output differs from the input by its capture state and depicted antibody association.

operations.information_effect: Selection operates through the RNA–polymerase association. It enriches the intended nascent RNA population, with antibody-dependent nonspecific capture possible; the drawn cap is not a separate cap-selection step.

method_scopes.rationale: The card names Churchman and Weissman 2011, and the matching primary abstract explicitly names NET-seq and its application in S. cerevisiae. The assigned row and standalone diagram support all three local operations. The poster labels the input RNAPII elongation complex, clarifying the standalone caption Transcriptome complex. The neighbouring mammalian row supplies no operations to this scope. Primary content inspection is limited to the registered abstract: antibody identity, library-end chemistry and a complete 2011 protocol are not claimed as verified.
